limitations: Pending orders (backlog): Counts orders created in the 30 days before each point in time that had no dispatched timestamp yet at that time.

Units moved counts tran_qty for picking transaction types only (Pick (201)), so each unit is counted once. Moves, replenishment, put-away, loading, reversals and adjustments are excluded. Shipping types are not added, to avoid counting picked units a second time.
Order counts are distinct per hour and summed, so an order that reaches the same stage in two different hours is counted twice.
Timestamps are read as the warehouse's local time (Asia/Kolkata).
No external data (weather, traffic, transport, events) is used; causes outside the warehouse database cannot be assessed.

items.statement: Warehouse transactions: 1,376 transactions today up to 13:00.
Units moved: 1,995 units today up to 13:00.
Orders received: 531 orders today up to 13:00.
Orders picked: 435 orders today up to 13:00.
Orders packed: 389 orders today up to 13:00.
Orders loaded: 306 orders today up to 13:00.
Orders dispatched: 246 orders today up to 13:00.
Order processing time: 102 minutes today up to 13:00.
Pending orders (backlog): 285 orders today up to 13:00.
Orders dispatched is −11.5% against a baseline of 278 orders (median of the same weekday in previous weeks, over the same hours, 5 comparable periods).
Orders dispatched is 3.7 standard deviations below its historical mean for this window — significant deterioration.
Pending orders (backlog) also shows significant deterioration (+22.3%).
Warehouse WH-B accounts for 98% of the total dispatch shortfall (−47.3% against its own baseline).
Other warehouses: WH-A −0.8%, WH-C +14.5%.
Within warehouse WH-B, order stage changes against baseline: dispatch −47.3%, loading −22.1%, packing −2.4%, picking −2.2%.
The largest observed decline in warehouse WH-B is in dispatch (−47.3%).
Hourly comparison for warehouse WH-B: dispatch has been on the adverse side of its hourly baseline from 09:00 and still is.
By category in warehouse WH-B: 'Parcel' accounts for 44% of the shortfall (−64.5%).
Pending orders are +22.3% against their baseline, which is consistent with orders accumulating rather than a drop in demand. This is an interpretation, not a verified cause.
The available warehouse data shows a significant dispatch decline concentrated in warehouse WH-B, beginning around 09:00, but the available data is insufficient to determine the underlying cause.
